title: Photogrammetry & 3D Reconstruction
summary: How ordinary photographs are converted into precise 3D models.

scenes.title: Photos to 3D: The Magic of Photogrammetry
scenes.narration: Photogrammetry transforms ordinary 2D photos into precise 3D models, capturing complex shapes and textures. It's like giving a computer human-like depth perception, enabling digital twins of real-world objects.

scenes.title: Triangulation: How Depth is Perceived
scenes.narration: Like our eyes, photogrammetry uses multiple overlapping photos from different angles to find common points. By knowing the camera's position for each photo, it can triangulate the precise 3D location of these points.

scenes.title: The 3D Reconstruction Pipeline
scenes.narration: The process starts with feature detection and matching across images, followed by bundle adjustment to refine camera parameters and generate a sparse point cloud. Finally, a dense point cloud is created, then meshed and textured.

scenes.title: Real-World Applications: From Maps to VR
scenes.narration: Photogrammetry is crucial for geospatial mapping, creating accurate 3D maps of cities and terrain. It's also vital for cultural heritage preservation, digitizing historical sites like Pompeii for study and virtual tours.

scenes.title: Future Impact: Digital Twins & Beyond
scenes.narration: Photogrammetry enables the creation of detailed digital twins for industries like manufacturing and urban planning, allowing virtual testing and monitoring. This technology is rapidly evolving, driving innovations in robotics and augmented reality.
